[h1]They killed a classic[/h1] WOW. When I saw that [i]Chrono Trigger[/i] came out on Steam I was stoked. I love this game. It’s one of my favourite games which I’ve played on SNES, PS1 & DS & I bought the soundtrack when the anniversary happened in Japan. And, even though I hate the lag on opening menus in the PS1 version, each time they released it I felt completely comfortable buying it. I thought the overwhelmingly negative reviews for this version had to be an exaggeration, but I couldn't have been more wrong. [b]It takes a special kind of laziness and greed to kill a classic this unceremoniously[/b].  The UI is disgusting, with random buttons all over the screen at a different resolution from the main visuals, because this is so clearly just a mobile port that they tossed up on Steam in order to con fans. The font is absolutely disgusting. Gone is the fun pixelated text that we’ve been looking at for 23 years. The battle menu is both disjointed and strange looking. Even the audio is fucked. Half of the menu interaction sounds are muted…  Everything about this is trash. Not only are the visuals all weirdly washed out, but you can see clear seams in sprites and the backgrounds which were not present in other versions; it has weird frame lag at random times; going from the main window to the map screen feels like looking at 2 completely different resolutions (because it probably is…). It is amazing to me what a visual downgrade this game has received over 2 decades after its release.  This entire thing would be incredibly shameful, but after what SquEnix did to Deus Ex, Hitman, and Secret of Mana, what the fuck should we expect? Why don’t they just go full-on Konami, and switch from making games to cramming their IP into pachi-slot machines.  I never thought that a [i]Chrono Trigger[/i] game could piss me off.  [b]**REFUNDED**[/b]

Let me start by saying Chrono Trigger is a timeless RPG, one of the best out there. The story is captivating, the characters unique and interesting, the battle mechanics revolutionary for the time without sacrificing flexibility, the time travel aspect of the game is ingenuous and excelently executed, the graphics are stunning and the score is heavenly.  Of course not all is perfect with the game, it has its share of flaws; even more so in the new zones added in the DS version, the contrast between old and new level design is big.  All around Chrono Trigger is a must have for any RPG fans...   With this in mind I can't possibly recomend this port of the game. It's not broken as in unplayable, but there are features that definetively will let down even the most hardcore fans of the game. Not only the text looks awful, but in some cutscenes it doesn't even load correctly, giving you almost no time to read whatever the characters are saying, if you want to rename a character an awful windows text box screen appears, and there are some minor aspects of the game that are plain broken and unplayable, making it impossible to accomplish some minor, and optional, events.   If you're like me and want to experience this game regardless of the quality of the port, go ahead and buy it (or better, borrow it from a friend), but if you're not, then you'd better steer clear from this mess and wait until SE releases the port -- or remaster/remake we deserve.

Oh dear. I pre-ordered this game the moment I heard of it. What a great concept! Whenever I played SimCity or Cities: Skylines I always thought - 'something's missing'. Mayors are not dictators; they're constrained by constantly changing political circumstances and harassed by often viscious opposition parties. So a city game with the political element sounded ideal. Unfortunately I don't think I've ever been more disappointed by a game.  The developer clearly had a great idea but then struggled to realise it. The result is a flat, one-dimensional game that offers no depth either as a city builder or as a political simulator. The city building bit is ridiculously simplistic - drag and drop your district and, boom, you're done. The political simulation is equally simplistic. You want something? Ask the City Council for it and then 'influence' the parties - i.e. perform the same repetitive clicks over and over again - until they let you have it. It's too easy.  The different parties have no depth to them. I don't get the impression of dealing with a complex, roiling mass of confliciting political ambition like an actual city council would be. You don't even get to know the names of the party leaders - which is odd as the game is supposedly character-driven. They're just sort of... there. The bias towards socialist policies is also obvious and irritating.  Game mechanics are frustrating, too. The only thing you can really do to actually build your city, apart from place districts, is place services. These are crazy expensive so you can't place many and rather than their effectiveness being tied to how many people can reach them on the street - like most services in Cities: Skylines for example - there's a ridiculous radial influence that just leads you to bunch everything in the centre where it will reach more people.  Graphics, too, are poor. There isn't a feeling of a living, breathing city but of a dull, slow collection of pixels.  I could go on but in short - save your money (also - £35!!! Jog on). My only hope is that now this idea is out there, some other developer will turn it into a worthy game.

[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/7871885/]Follow our curator page:[b] OCG-Curations[/b] if you like and want to see more reviews like this one.[/url][/quote]  [u]Rating[/u]  [b]7.5/10[/b]  [u]Pros:[/u]  Fun Gameplay Good Vehicle Editor Steam Workshop Support Enjoyable, Short Campaign Free Demo  [u]Cons:[/u]  Some Parts could use better tooltips Controls can be a bit frustrating Poor Performance  [h1]Overview[/h1]  “Trailmakers” is a game designed to harness a player’s creativity. The game has three game modes: Expedition, Race, and Sandbox. Expedition is a short campaign that also works as a tutorial. The player follows along a predetermined path that gives players access to new, more powerful parts as they get further. The player doesn’t have to always follow the path, and there are plenty of small areas with optional challenges. These challenges also include parts that can’t be grabbed on the main road. Sandbox allows the player to build without limitations. Thankfully, there are also challenges sprinkled around the Sandbox landscape to test out any of the player’s creations. Finally, race has the player building the fastest car or plane to beat a time record. Races can also be played against other players as well. The player does not have to go alone though, as there are numerous multiplayer modes including Sandbox. The graphics in this title are a cartoonish science fiction style. This works quite well for the setting of an alien planet. Unfortunately, the performance leaves a bit to be desired at the game’s current stage of development. Large objects and the small explosive devices will pop-up at random in front of the player which makes driving at high speeds more of a chore than it needs to be.      [h1]In DepthGame Breakdown[/h1] [u]Gameplay:[/u]  [b]Vehicle Building:[/b] The main gameplay mechanic in this game is the ability to build vehicles of various sizes and shapes. The way that this starts is by entering building mode. This is accomplished by pressing the “b” key. This will lift up any vehicles currently nearest to the player if there is any nearby. Otherwise the player has a blank slate to work with. The first part that must be placed is the vehicle seat. This is the place that the player will enter and is required to make a vehicle drivable. Blocks may then be attached to any of the connection points on the seat block. Blocks attach to the connection points based upon how the player is looking at the vehicle being built upon. There isn’t much of a build limit, and in Expedition mode the only blocks that are limited are the engine blocks. The problem with adding too many blocks is that every block adds weight.   [b]Vehicle Physics and Controls:[/b] Weight not only creates more mass which, in turn, slows down a vehicle overall, but it also can unbalance a vehicle. This would make a vehicle heavy on one side which the realistic physics will just flip over constantly. The physics are the reason that planes are hard to build and control properly. The problem with these physics is that every vehicle must be extremely well balanced or mirrored, or else they will be extremely difficult to control. There are different tires that grip different surfaces better, but when I was using my simple car in Expedition mode, I would spin crazily, which was quite frustrating. Especially while trying to complete some objectives.  [b]Game Modes:[/b] There are three main single player game modes in “Trailmakers”. They are: Expedition, Sandbox, and Race. Expedition is the campaign mode of the game. Unfortunately, it is quite easy and is rather short if rushed through. It does act as a great tutorial though for players just starting out with the game. I wish the Expedition did explain the best uses of a part through a better tooltip. I would also enjoy if Expedition had more story associated with it. The player doesn’t really know why they are stranded on an alien planet with an endless supply of metal vehicle parts. It seems like wasted potential currently. Sandbox mode is exactly as anyone would expect it to be. It is a giant space that allows a player to build any vehicle they like without limits. There are also some unlockable parts and challenges that can be completed to unlock said parts. The player is also unable to die, so nose diving a plane going over 500 mph can be a fun diversion.  [b]Overall:[/b] This is a fun game that is great for people that love to build and be creative. This title could use some work though, so only buy it knowing that this isn’t the final, feature complete product.   [u]Sound:[/u] The sound design in this game is exceptional. Engines makes satisfying and realistic noises which helps add to the game’s immersion. The suspension is one of the best sound effects included in the game. If the player is bouncing on the suspension springs, a spring sound will occur and even when the action ends abruptly, the sound doesn’t cut off poorly. The music in the game is serviceable, but in a game that requires planning and concentration, the music may be the first thing that the player turns off.    [u]Graphics:[/u]  The graphics in this game are a cartoonish sci-fi theme. What I enjoyed about this game is the scale. The small player character is tiny in comparison to the hulking, monstrous vehicles that they have built. The graphics are nice and look quite beautiful on high.   [u]Performance:[/u]  Performance in this game is something that could use some more work. My FPS stuttered in this title at the highest graphics settings when I don’t have any problems with the highest settings of games like “Warframe” and upscaled “Dota 2”.  One of the worst offenders of the performance is the pop-in of objects. While I was driving quickly, large mountains would pop into view. The small, alien, explosive plants also suffer from this object pop-in. This makes cars that I built frustrating to play sometimes because I would have to replay a section of Expedition multiple times just to dodge these plants. Finally, the options menu doesn’t have many options in it at all. Keys can’t be remapped and certain graphical aspects can’t be changed.

I don't really know what to write in this review, I am a huge fan of Behemoth, (I mean look at my profile) but I can't say that I enjoyed most of my time playing, in fact, my playtime as I write this review is incredibly little for me, when I get a new game I can easily spend 20 hours on it or more in a week.  I was hyped for this game, and when it was released into Early Access I wanted to get it immediately, but I forgot later, and when I eventually did buy it was more because it was a Behemoth game than anything else.  Probably my biggest problem with the game is it's not quite as action-packed as most Behemoth games are, this tends to be slow, and the entire gameplay is moving your characters and then your characters do whatever they want. Essentially gameplay is slow and not too engaging, it feels like an incredibly simple board game, it might NOT be incredibly simple but it certainly seems like it. Also, combat and overall gameplay is incredibly repetitive.  Despite being an open-world, their doesn't seem to be much to do, in this game you can pick a quest that has little amusing cutscenes explaining the situation, then you fight. And the combat just isn't enjoyable for me, because again, it's simply selecting a character and moving them. Exploration seems fairly bland to me, the world feels almost randomly generated, being open plains with tree/mountain/buildings/water that have no seemingly real significance besides being things you need to walk around. I'd go so far as to say exploring in Castle Crashers and Battleblock Theater was more interesting. In Castle Crashers you could go through a level, find a cool new weapon, blow up walls to find hidden rooms, or even bring that one bird that finds secrets. In Battleblock Theater you could find secret rooms, and walls that looked real but you could actually walk through, leading you to treasure like gems or yarn.  Treasure is also interesting in Pit People, as far as I know, there is: -New units. -New Cosmetics/Armor. -New Weapons.  It seems to me from my time playing that Pit People has the most character customization, but personally with the different types of weapons and armor I think they overdid it, it's been a while, but I remember lots of different options for armor and weapons. I believe there is like 3 types of shields, 3 types of helmets, a few different types of bows and swords. Seems kind of like a lot for a game so simple. In my opinion, Battleblock Theater actually did weapons really well, weapons are so incredibly different there are lots of things you can do with each one. (Freezing ice or exploding frogs?) Unlike Pit People in my opinion, where you can trade a light shield for a slightly bigger shield. (And yes I am aware that these have minor differences, you know what I mean.)  The humor, possibly the most important thing. Hmm. When I played the game, I was amused for most of the experience, but nothing sticks out as a particularly funny moment and I actually don't recall laughing at all. I won't pretend to be a humor expert, but I didn't laugh.   I think it's cool that Behemoth has decided to branch out a bit from their usual (beat-em-up?) games, but personally it's not my cup of tea so far. Maybe it will be though, the game is still in Early Access, right? I don't really think I'd recommend this game unfortunately, I really do love Behemoth, but this game isn't something I'd recommend to someone (But I'd still encourage them to try it anyway) who: A: Enjoyed previous Behemoth games. B: Enjoys strategy games.  As I haven't said much of anything positive in this review, I'm going to have to not recommend it. Which is causing me physical pain, I love Behemoth, and I'll try this game again sometime.  If I remember more things I will update this review.

Wow... Just wow. What happened?  I'd like to start by saying I was an early access player. As someone who just now discovered this game you might think it's content filled, a fully finished game, and my hours playing it justifies how much game you can get out of it... Wrong. I erased my old early access review thinking it wouldn't be relevant anymore, but I couldn't be more wrong.  Not only was the development cycle of this game all over the place, so is the community.  To start, Pit People isn't a horrible game but it definitely isn't great. If you like turn based strategy or The Behemoth's typical humor you will most likely enjoy this game...at first. When stepping into Pit People you have this incredible feeling of exploration and a deep combat system with nearly infinite unlocks and collectables. However after a few hours the game is bare-boned and shallow as they come.   Firstly, the classes of characters in this game are not developed and balanced enough. They don't feel unique enough and when putting them in raw combat to compare they all pretty much play out the same. There really isn't a strategy aspect to the game as it stands and I don't think it ever will. Your party will almost always be able to take on 2 encounters before having to heal or return back to the hub. If you're great or if you're terrible it always takes about 2 battles to make you need to retreat. This game gets incredibly stale after your 10th battle; they're all the same despite what enemies are present and how many there are. It is very clear The Behemoth is doing trial and error on this one as they go. The strategy aspect of this game is absent.  Secondly, the map and it's exploration. This game has about 5-6 maps in which each time you load into a new world it picks a spawn point on one of those 6 maps. There's really no point to this aspect of the game. I was fine with it at first but after updates they removed the beacon back to the city. Also, Hats off to Nvizzio for keeping in touch with the community and rolling out updates as quickly as they can. With all of that said, I'll list my pro and cons.  Pros -Coaster editor/maker in this game is EXCELLENT, Sure its a bit finnicky sometimes, but it's damn good and can only get better, I prefer it to the piece by piece editor in PC, it's one thing I hated about RCT3.  -Decent variety of scenery to start and I'm sure this will be expanded upon -Solid amount of flat ride content with a new one coming every 2 weeks in Major patches (Yes, I believe them, they have stuck to that schedule so far) -I'll probably be crucified for this, but after the latest update..graphics have improved markedly, and I'd expect that to continue -The Management aspect is there, could be better but it's decent for EA. -Terrain tools are easy to use and effective, need an option for underground building though. -There is more but I'll leave it at that for now, new update is scheduled to be rolled out Tuesday or Wednesday next week so I'll edit this review at that time  Cons -Peeps need work (Animations/texture/etc) -Optimization at this point is a bit shaky, people across a wide array of system are getting mixed results, once the park gets large it really starts to slow down, apparently this is getting addressed in next patch, I'll update if that is the case -Pathing is shoddy at the moment. -AI behavior is pretty poor in the current build, mechanics don't always fix rides, janitors are slow, etc. -Water quality sucks. lol. -Can't change ingame graphics while in your park. (Seriously guys?) -Can't place scenery on elevated paths (Again, really guys?) -Coaster ratings need work, every coaster I make is a vomit comet -General bugs and such  -Overall, I'd recommend this based on the rate it is improving and the committment Nvizzio has shown to the franchise. Great game whether you are a RTS fan or just have an interest in WW II. You build your deck from one of 18 divisions present at Normandy recreated using the historical TO&E. At any one time you probably control what amount to a small battalion of infantry, tanks, artillery, and even air support. Maps are great and were apparently created using aerial photos of the battlefields as they appeared in WW II. I think the game excels at capturing the spirit of the hedgerow fighting where every field and every hedgerow was turned into a small fortress. Learning to properly reconnoiter, manage line of sight, and employ combined arms is essential. You can micro as much as you want; not as much as in a squad based tactics game, but your units can survive on their own without needing to constantly babysit them. Firefights look and sound gorgeous, zoom in on a fight and turn your volume up, you won't regret it. There should be three campaigns to play offline and I think the AI is a noticeable step up from Wargame's.   Cons: Needs further optimization could run smoother, but it is a beta and improvements are in the works.   Running the game can be a heavy load on you processor, however mine is only clocked at 2.4ghz, but I can still run the game on high settings.  Final opinion: Some of the best fun I've had in a long time and one of the best RTS I have ever played, even though it's still in beta.

(I give this game a 9/10) After the disappointing last few games, it really seemed that each subsequent game took away at least one or two things that made previous games fun. WWE 2K17 with the lack of any great modes, and WWE 2K18 with the lack of any "wow factor" or improvements, which sort of made the experience less great and more stale than what one would hope. This game finally breaks that trend, as it is one of the best WWE games since the 7th generation. Not to say this game is perfect, as there are still a few problems, but the improvements made here make it a mostly amazing experience. The visuals, while not drastically different from 2K18, is more detailed this time around, the gameplay is much faster and much more fun, the payback system is pretty great to see a return here, the roster is mostly amazing, the My Career mode is actually fantastic, the return of 2K Showcase mode is also amazing, the WWE Universe mode has more options and actually feels like an evolution from WWE 2K17 (unlike 2K18's), the creation suite is amazing and better than ever with the ability to make a MITB briefcase and a Minecraft-esque wrestler, and the overall presentation is top notch. It really seems like 2K and Yukes have listened to their fans, because this just might be the best WWE 2K game on the 8th gen systems so far. However, this still isn't without it's flaws. The roster, while still great, has a few less legends than previous years, the commentary is still kind of bad, the soundtrack, in my opinion, isn't as good as 2K18's, and a few classic arenas have been removed as well. I get that many people, especially nowadays, want to focus more on current superstars, but, as a WWE Legends fan, there's a bit less than what I was hoping for in terms of that. But, these gripes aren't anywhere near enough to keep me from loving this game, which is something I couldn't have said with previous WWE 2K games, and I absolutely recommend it to any wrestling fan who hasn't checked it out yet, because even if you're a bit skeptical after the previously mentioned disappointing games, there's no need to be, as this is a huge step in the right direction.

Originally released in 1997, [i] Age of Empires [/i] was the first game in the [i] Age of Empires [/i] series, followed by an expansion pack, [i] The Rise of Rome [/i], the following year. This game, the [i] Definitive Edition [/i], is a fully updated re-release of the original game and its expansion.  This game is a historical RTS covering a massive span of human history, roughly from the end of the last Ice Age to the fall of the Roman Empire. It contains multiple sprawling campaigns, each of which should take between 6-12 hours to complete, plus the option to play skirmish games against AI opponents. It also contains online multiplayer and a scenario editor, but I have little experience with either, and so will not discuss them in this review.   On the positive side, the game looks gorgeous, and the remastered soundtrack is pleasant without becoming grating. The campaigns are fun, and are generally challenging without suffering from the unpredictable and infuriating difficulty spikes that plagued those in the original game. The AI can put up a substantial challenge to the player, and actual strategy is often required to win. Although all factions share the same overall set of technologies, units, and buildings, no faction has access to all of them. This, combined with various faction bonuses (ex. gold miners work 15% faster), ensures that no two factions feel exactly the same.  On the negative side, unit animations are somewhat stiff, and unit pathfinding can often be atrocious, requiring the player to effectively "babysit" their units. The AI, while capable, often relies on spamming one or two unit types, forcing the player to spend a large amount of time fighting off whack-a-mole raids.  Overall, [i] Age of Empires: Definitive Edition [/i] is an excellent remake of what I feel to be an unjustly forgotten classic RTS. If you love RTS games, ancient history, or both, pick this one up.

app_name: Ni no Kuni™ II: Revenant Kingdom
representative_review: I enjoyed aspects of this game, but there were a few issues  that would prevent me from fully recommending it to everyone.  I did enjoy enough aspects to still tip this to a thumbs up especially for fans of the jRPG genre.  Here are the things I really liked:  + I loved that it was lighthearted.  Some  RPGs can get very heavy-handed in their angst and almost become depressing so this was a welcome change of pace.  + The story-book aesthetic was awesome and the music was also amazing!  The artistic  representation could not have been better.   + The combat was fun, it is true to other Level 5 titles such as Rogue Galaxy back on the PS2.  + In theory, kingdom building should be fun and was to a certain point (I'll get back to this)  + Army battles were an interesting idea that was decently well executed and a fun way to break up the game play loop.  There are a few times you need to do it for story purposes but not too often.  Now come the things that were some near deal breakers.  - Sloppy world building.  There was a lot of potential here and a lot of things just weren't that well fleshed out.  Many kingdoms just felt like a checklist item with no real history in how they relate to their world other than the first kingdom that serves as a central plot point (kind of).  - 'Meh' character development.  Most were popular tropes that you'd expect to find with kind of bland writing. [spoiler]  I felt that most were static characters who lacked any real growth during the narrative with the exception of Evan and sort of Roland, but pretty much everyone else was just kind of there and didn't really grow or change much which is strange considering the scope of their journey. [/spoiler]   - Difficulty jumps.  This game isn't really difficult by any means, but it is irritating to be over-leveled in one territory then move to the next and be under-leveled by 5-10 levels.  Even then you can hack and slash your way through enemies that are 10+ levels above you so long as you have good gear but it was an odd design choice.  - Forced kingdom building. I almost quit because of this and almost put this to a negative review. Mouse over the spoiler area to see why and also a quick tip on how to avoid that particular frustration should you choose to buy the game.  [spoiler]  I got to the very end of the game and it blocks you from going into the last encounters until your kingdom and certain buildings are upgraded.  Take some time to upgrade to at least Kingdom Level 3 to avoid this.  Fortunately, I had done some upgrading already but it took me a few hours of extra grinding to get past this point.  There was no good reason to force this on the player, especially after building up the impending final confrontation.  It killed the pacing of the narrative stopping the  story in its tracks to go chasing after side quests which were largely fetch quests. [/spoiler]    If you decide to play this game there are a lot of fun elements but because of the issues I mentioned I would wait for a sale (It tends to go on sale pretty often).

app_name: Ni no Kuni™ II: Revenant Kingdom
representative_review: I loved playing Ni No Kuni 2, much better than the first game. It's various mechanics are well thought out, introduced as you progress, and they blended nicely into the story. The graphics are gorgeous, I would love seeing a "Tales of" game again in this pure anime-like cell-shading style. It's one of few games where I also spent a lot of time doing most of the optional sidequests. Rare for me nowadays, but here it felt very rewarding. After playing 58h I'll probably give it a couple of more hours for optional content, and then leave it resting, and probably picking it up again once DLCs are released.  Before buying I was very sceptical about whether it would be too child-like for me to enjoy, being used to more adult-like RPGs. But the scepticism was unfounded. Behing the nice facade, the topics covered are quite serious, the overall story much enjoyable. Coupled with the gameplay this game was way better than expected.  Only downside for me was that the dialogues weren't fully voiced. Only the main cutscenes are. It's also quite weird that there are some dialogues which are only partly voiced, voice stopping/starting in the middle. But that's criticism on a high level.  It ran flawlessly on my PC. A well made PC version. In all the time only a couple of crashes, nothing serious because there's autosave.  I would say, definitely go with it and purchase!

app_name: Ni no Kuni™ II: Revenant Kingdom
representative_review: You ever meet someone who is just so beautiful and attractive, and you get to know them and they're kind of a dick, maybe not intollerable but definitely not very favorable? Kinda how I feel about this game.  This game is absolutely and incredibly stylish and beautiful without a doubt, but there's an ungodly plethera of annoyances that made me have no motivation to continue after ~22 hours and so close to the end.  I desperately wanted to like this game and kept pushing through, but there's so little of value here except for how pretty it is. If you need an example about how visuals aren't what make the game, here ya go y'all.  PROS: - Phenomenal visuals - Good voice acting (sometimes can be annoying) - Nice variety of scenery in some locations - Average but lacking combat - Pretty nice animations - Okay sound design  CONS: - Uninteresting and sometimes predictable story - Combat can be sluggish & is pretty basic for an action RPG; Attacks don't feel very impactful - Obnoxious and boring RTS-lite gameplay segments - Boring characters & next to no character development - Very slow movement throughout the map for many hours of the game - Kinda unbalanced within the characters; I mainly used Roland b/c his massive range w/ skills & because they're so powerful and cover so much ground, kinda neglected many of the other characters because of how inferior they were to him - Tacky and horrendous soundtrack throughout much of the game (especially in Goldpaw, jesus christ) - Awful stuttering issue on PC (not sure if it was fixed since I last played)  Like I said earlier, I really wanted to like this game but I just can't.  I guess a 6/10? Idk, I don't want to think about this game anymore.

app_name: Ni no Kuni™ II: Revenant Kingdom
representative_review: I've never played Ni No Kuni 1, but always wanted to due to the graphical style (I'm a big Ghibli fan) and the voice acting. It seemed like an RPG of a Ghibli movie. When 2 came out, I really liked the idea of kingdom building combined with what I thought would be a game just like 1. I enjoy Cities: Skylines and other sims, so why not!  Unfortunately, this game was a huge disappointment. To be fair, I don't play many JRPGs, so maybe these are characteristic of the genre, I don't know. They story is shallow and disjointed, the characters look great due to the art style, but have basically 0 character development, there is almost no voice acting outside a few lines (and the dialogue that's there is bland and boring - Pillars of Eternity this is not), the 'cinematic' cut scenes are short and unexciting, the combat is over within 10 seconds most times and *extremely* easy - I could put the controller down for most combat and let my AI companions kill everything - and the kingdom building is just grindy since there's no challenge to anything, but you HAVE to do it or be gated off from further content.  This was an extremely disappointing game. I never completed it, and I doubt I'll pick it up again. I am, however, still willing to pick up Ni No Kuni 1, since everything I read points to it being very different from this.

Really enjoying this game, when you come up with a plan and execute it well there's no greater feeling. Australian servers supported and aussie community seems great so far and very willing to communicate.  Guns seem decently balanced, gunplay isnt amazing but isnt bad either. Unlike siege flashbangs are actually useful (while still feeling fair) and also unlike siege it is nice to not have 60 characters whose abilities you should know to be able to compete at a high level.  The core gameplay excels where coordinating with your team is concerned. If you're not interested in teamwork this may not be a game for you. Flashing/smoking for your teammates, breaching at same times, covering angles for each other all feel really rewarding.  Tactics can be simple but also surprisingly deep. Feels juicy when you pull off a play the other team isnt expecting (like using your one wall charge on an interior wall directly to the objective while using smoke cover). Randomly generated maps always keep you on your toes in terms of coming up with plans of attack/defence and prevents hardened veterans from having a large map-knowledge advantage over newer players. It would however be better if it was unlimited randomly generated maps instead of 20 or so generated maps per week - if you play enough of the game you will play through all the maps that week leading to some repeats of layouts, but i understand that the devs do touch up the maps before they go live so makes sense that there isnt an infinite number.  Limited resources mean there's a lot of decision making as to when you want to use your more powerful weapons/equipment and when to save (which is also influenced by what map layout you get) and keeping track of what gear the enemy has used can be really helpful for strategising.  You can loot gear off fallen enemies and use it in the following rounds (if you survive) leading to fun strats like stealing an enemies breach charge detonating tool and trying to detonate the breach charge of an enemy as they deploy it the following round (boom!) or stealing attackers night vision goggles as defenders and turning off the lights the next round to give you the advantage.  Fun additions like the character versus screen when loading in and ability to name your squads really add to the experience as well (and honestly i wish they'd put the character versus screen between rounds as well as it's hilarious). Pixel art style is pretty neat in my opinion as well and i do enjoy the badass Judge Dredd-like cops vs. cyberpunk terrorists aesthetic.  Anyway probably sung praises enough, so will add that the game has crashed a couple of times and it can sometimes can be a little bit of effort to queue with friends as there are still some bugs with seeing invites that can set you back a few mins while you restart your game. Also i wasnt 100% sold on the game in my first 2 hrs playing as i hadn't fully worked out the gameplay and tactics but definitely felt hooked when i did and was willing to give callouts and teamworks a real shot.  To conclude - all in all a solid pick up for people who want a slightly faster paced, more tactical version of siege (and don't mind pixel graphics in a shooter haha)  tldr: many tactics, yes teamwork, fun game

If you're someone who in games like Diablo or PoE likes to spend hours and hours just planning their build and fine tuning equipment instead of "playing" the game, then Dragon Cliff might be a game for you. It automates the combat, and focuses on managing the adventurers and their skills and equipment.  Even though the combat is automated, the mechanics are quite involved, and that's what makes the game interesting. There's a wide variety of classes, skills, synergies and item effects, and a lot of different ways to build your team, and it's easy to respec and experiment with different builds. However some things like ancient devices, scrolls and amulet sets won't be unlocked until much later in the game.  I really enjoyed the game, but I have some complaints: - Performance is abysmal. It takes 10x more CPU and RAM than a game like this should. - Occasional crashes. Probably because it's 32-bit and runs out of memory. Fortunately there's autosave. - End game crafting is very tedious. You always have to wait to get the town buff for crafting, which runs out after 3-9 items, and then you have to wait again. And you might have to craft hundreds of items to get anything useful. - During combat there are no enemy stats visible. That makes it difficult to understand the game mechanics, especially the math involved in buff and debuff calculations.

Fun, but underwhelming.  When I grew up on the 16-Bit era of gaming, Secret Of Mana was the first major RPG i've played. It was fun, fast paced, had a good pace, great soundtrack, and some of the best graphics to offer at the time. I spent a lot of time playing it, and beat the game many times in the past.  Now, in 2018, I have had the opportunity to try the Remake of the game......And, really not much has changed....  Gameplay Secret Of Mana has always had a good formula of tatics of your weapons and magic, and leveling. In the SNES version, it was a very grindy experience. This was good and rewarding for the time because the lack of abiltiy to add more to the mechaincs. In this remake, nothing has really changed in that aspect. There isn't much invoation to the experience and the grinding is still there. This is still fun, but it also can get very boring over time to the point I need to take a break.  I was hoping this would of been maybe a little more modernized in today's time, but really i'm left with feeling like it was out to meet the status quo. The A.I suprisingly, remains to be as awful as the SNES game. Was this some intentional joke?   Sound  Sound is pretty good, on the classic music I mean. I really hate the remixes. I tried to listen to them in various places. The remixes are just awful for this game.  The voice acting (Japanese) isn't too bad. I hear voices i've heard before and they seem professional enough. I do like the fact all NPC's have voice acting, so that was a nice added touch.   Graphics.  Very underwhelming, and some may consider it an insult to a long time fanbase. It's not the worst graphical design i've ever seen, but it's not $40 good.  Some of the monster designs range from Ok, to kind of BAD. The character designs are nice at least. This really is a mobile tier level of design at a near AAA price on a remake.   Controls.  Controls work perfectly fine. No issues. No lockups. Smooth like butter.  Overall Secret Of Mana Remake is OKAY, and that's about it. It's not special, but not bad. It's great for the memories as an exerperience, but hollow for the design. This is a coat of paint on an old design. Grab this on a price drop, because it's hardly worth $40 in truth.   I recommend it for the good times it is, but be prepared to play just Secret Of Mana, with next to no innovation.    7.5/10.

Or hits actually register instead of hitting animation iframes all the damn time.  What this remake does is fix all of that, add a nice graphical overhaul (though higher res textures would've been nice) and a lovely rearranged soundtrack. Everything else is remarkably faithful down to some of the goofy animations and something I applaud. Some additional scenes were added to give the - let's be honest: fairly shallow - story and characters more depth without intruding. I could've done without the voice acting, but the Japanese dub is at least decent.  One big minus: No local or online coop despite the store page saying differently. I guess Squenix has tasted blood with the FF15 multiplayer DLC.

Hello boys and girls, adventure games fans of all ages! Do you love old school adventure games remniscent of Maniac Mansion, Monkey Island, and other classics? Then do we have a game for you! Enjoy Thimbleweed Park, a small town filled with.... interesting people and strange events. Help two bumbling FBI investigators seemingly solve a murder, and in the process of tracking down the culprit, meet the locals. Why, even the dead are lively in Thimbleweed Park! This is the adventure game of your dreams, folks.   Until you realize-- it isn't....  Holy crap, I've never played a game so promising, and then-- so bitterly disappointing. First off, I feel it only fair to list the positives:   1) Graphic style and mechanics are a beauiful love letter to old school adventure games. 2) You can play as five interesting characters. (Ransome the Clown was my favourite) 3) Lots of meta humour and gaming/pop culture references. 4. The town of Thimbleweed Park itself feels incredibly flushed out. You can tell that a lot of effort went into this game, which is why I have such a problem with what is the biggest NEGATIVE of the game.  That being said, lets get into the negatives:  1) The meta humour though at times really funny, grows to be a bit too much. New adventure gamers will not get a lot of the jokes, and I feel like the game relied too heavily on this particular brand of humour. 2) Puzzles were either too easy, or way too difficult and did not offer hints if needed. This may be the age of the internet, but it ruins the fun if you need a walkthrough too often. 3) NOT. ENOUGH. PUZZLES. IN. CASUAL. MODE. In the first playthrough of this game, I played with a friend who does not play a lot of point & click adventure games, so we played casual mode to ease him into things. Despite it being in casual mode, we did not expect this game to be so-- easy. Things were just given to you a lot of the time. You didn't have to work for them. There were also complete chunks of story that were missing. Just because you're in casual mode, doesn't mean the game should be so simple. Put some challenges in there too.  Lastly, negative # 4.... this is the most important: THE ENDING WAS ABYSMAL.  At first, my buddy and I thought it was a joke... no. No. it was not. With the exception of Life is Strange, I have never been so pumped for a game, and so completely disappointed and angry by the end. Was it really necessary to make the ending meta too? I felt like the developers had used up all of their creativity a flatlined near the end, so they just decided, "Okay, let's just do this because it's cheap, easy, and I'm tired. Gamers won't mind! It's already enough like an old school adventure game... right?" Just because it's easy doesn't mean you should go with it. Why couldn't the game be a cool little murder mystery with the culprit revealed based upon your actions during gameplay? Instead we got the most stereotypical, cop out ending imaginable. When I discovered this game and who was behind its creation. I immediately thought it would be worthwhile. Wrong!  The game is solid from a story standpoint until you realize what's happening... then you become a little angry because you wasted your money on something that could have been great, had a little more effort gone into it. A lot of time was spent playing as these characters, and roaming around the town. Near the end, I didn't care what happened to the characters, and neither did the developers, apparently. My friend and I were so disappointed and angry, we wanted to leave the game. For this reason, I cannot in good conscience, recommend Thimbleweed Park.  If you must buy it, buy it on sale.  Even then, I suggest it only to the most dedicated of adventure game fans.  If you are dying to try an adventure game, I recommend the Monkey Island Series, Day of the Tentacle, Broken Sword 1 & 2, Grim Fandango, and pretty much anything by Daedalic Productions. Those are just a few.  I give Thimbleweed Park a barely squeak by rating of 4.9\10 it starts out fun at first, but becomes a festering boil by the end. Moral of the story: I will now pay more attention to the negative reviews of games

[b]Senran Kagura: Estival Versus[/b] is a great game marred by a weak story and some misguided gameplay choices. If you're new to the series you should absolutely play [url=store.steampowered.com/app/889510]Burst Re:Newal[/url] and [url=store.steampowered.com/app/411830]Shinovi Versus[/url] first as they have much more serious stories and less flawed combat.  With that out of the way, Estival Versus features a massive cast of 35 characters, basically everyone, plus it introduces Sayuri (Asuka's grandmother and Hanzō's wife) who's playable in both her old and young forms, Ryōki (Ryōbi and Ryōna's dead sister) as well as the 3 Mikagura sisters. Basically all 4 main ninja schools get sucked into a pocket dimension by Sayuri and forced to participate in a summer festival of sorts. The story is mostly lighthearted fanservice (just like those beach episodes in anime shows) plus all the same in-jokes and running gags with the more serious content put at the very end. The game doesn't bother reintroducing anyone, if you don't know a particular's character backstory it will just not make sense to you. Why is Homura a master of impersonations? Why is Imu a boxer? Why does Murasaki talk with her teddy bear? Etc, etc. If you're a fan and know the answers then this game is for you.  The story mode is no longer split into different schools, there are 57 story missions played across 9 chapters + 5 personal missions for each of 27 girls, and then there are also dual missions + special missions available as DLC. It's a lot of content and it's going to take you at least 40 hours to clear everything.  Now the elephant in the room is the gameplay. They changed the system completely from Shinovi Versus in an attempt to make the game more technical. It's a lot slower and there are long delay animations on almost every action, even a simple transition from running to standing still has a long delay. Sure, it's not too bad, you can get used to it, but the thing is they made the heavy characters (Katsuragi, Yomi, Yozakura, Murasaki, Hanabi) incredibly slow and they're just garbage to play compared to fast and snappy characters like Yumi or Hikage. Especially since even the basic grunts now have numerous status inflicting/stunlocking attacks. Good luck winding up an attack as Yomi if there are some archers in the back. And then the loli characters (Hibari, Mirai, Minori, Kafuru) were made incredibly weak, they can spam a lot of attacks but barely do any damage. You think, okay I'll just save up some ninja scrolls and spam specials, but the AI often responds with their own special which renders them invincible, meaning it negates your attack completely and you waste the scrolls. It's a fun game when the story has you play as the "good" characters like Homura, Hikage, Yumi, Asuka etc, but if you get stuck with Kafuru and her water guns it's very, very frustrating. It's astounding how horrible the character balance is in this game, especially given the fact that it has a multiplayer mode. They did fix all of this in Burst Re:Newal, but sadly Estival Versus never received a balance patch.  Now, it's not all that bad, there are some cool gameplay additions exclusive to Estival Versus, such as an AI partner system for some missions (you can even do combined aerial raves), bombs (consumable items that range from fire/ice/electric grenades to being able to summon your own grunts to fight on your side) as well as... mechs. Yes, you can ride a Gundam like mech, fly around a level and blast the hell out of everyone.  They also added creative finishers which are like stage fatalities from Mortal Kombat except without the fatal part. If you defeat a girl near one of the hotspots it will trigger a special animation where the girl is stripped naked and molested by the scenery in some embarrassing way. There are 50+ completely unique and gorgeously animated creative finishers in the game, it's a feast for the eyes.  The soundtrack is probably the best in the series. Just listen to [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EUkSi6TFrPE]this[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y0U9piUio5s]this[/url] or [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f384kbZMlUY]this[/url]. It's really good.  Overall, the game features an obscene amount of content, a massive cast of characters, numerous outfits and accessories. If you want to overdose on Senran Kagura, then this will be your guilty pleasure.

Good: - improved graphics, - more girls, more maps, more costumes, more accessories, more DLC (hurr), - big improvements to dressing room, - ultimates no longer require low health.   Bad: - The combat is absolutely infuriating, not only did they not fix issues from previous game but they geniunely made it worse, - combat was made painfully SLOOOOOOOOOOOOOOW, coming into this game straight after Sinovi Versus it hit me like a truck, there is now delay on every move be it attack , dodge, jump or even running and it feels awful, - constantly being stunned/frozen/interrupted/unable to move - because if there is one thing I want in my hack & slash is to not be able to hack or slash... It is okay to pushing players with CC occasinally for some really bad moves but this game hands out CC like candy - camera is awful, if you ever get fighting next to a wall you wont be seeing a thing, - AI shinobi blatantly cheat with ungodly levels of stagger immunity, while you will get interrupted and stunned just form them looking in your general direction, extra fun when every second mission sees you fighting 3 at once.... I do intend to finish the story mode at least as I hate dropping games but I will be very unlikely to pick up next Versus game unless I see some proper rework of combat. I want fun not frustration. Spoilers to the ending & How I think it could've been better; [spoiler]Riding along after you've just completed another puzzle,  your Okomotive is fully upgraded and you're ready for anything. Explosions sound off in the distance, then disaster. The Okomotive breaks in half, The forward section is damaged, but can still move. You travel as far as you can till your vehicle goes no further. [u]You light a fire. Fade to black.[/u][/spoiler] What? What was our protagonist trying to achieve? Why did they waste all their time for that? How about; You travel as far as you can till your vehicle goes no further. Our protagonist reluctantly abandons ship and starts walking off. After a while, they slow down. They give up and burry the head in the sand. They've lost everything and have nothing, with no hope of salvation. A figure apears ([spoiler]you never see another person in the game[/spoiler]), They help you get up and guide you to their vehicle/home. The structure lights up. Fade to black.  Yeah, it's not perfect, but it's better than what you get, and something actually happens.  My final thoughts; A fun game to play, A horrible story to watch.

Like the sandbox that won't let you play threw all the eras. If they combined Transport Fever and this together, then you would have just a great game. Though like this it is just a big loss, because of those limitations that make me not to start up the game again.

Review proper: Dont mind the jim sterling fanboys, the game is not bad BUT, its not a straight up warriors game, as it has more in common with bladestorm and kessen than the core DW series, feeling more like a spin off (specially with all the stuff they experiment with) than a main game.  gameplay: Its less of a beat-em up and more (VERY) light strategy with how it handle things, with a massive focus on actually moving your frontline and alies into combat properly; you can try to do everything alone, but even mooks will swarm and agressively attack you if you do, helping your army get to where you need it is everything, so they can keep other enemies and mooks off you while you fight important enemies directly (which is, admitingly, a bit on the easy side, though, again, it gets balanced with how agressive mooks and other officers can be) the combat itself is now focused almost entirelly on positioning and keeping enemies combo-ed in a way that they cant counter, and is, at its very basic, simplified from the regular series.  Writing and plot: writing, presentation and characterisation wise this is one of the best dw games so far, with characters actually having good and believeable interactions and details, for the most part, handled very well; if you are in the series for the characters and settings, this is a MUST get, as exploring the beautifully crafted world is fun, even if said world is rather amateurish when it comes to open worlds.  World:  the world looks beautiful, but feels empty and could have been better realized when in towns, vilalges or when everything works, it looks and feels great but otherwise it feels like it could have been done better.

app_name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel II
representative_review: This was a great RPG, but I feel a little bit let down when I compare it to the first game. The first game had deliberately slow pacing, which gave time for the characters to develop in meaningful ways. The pacing of Trails of Cold 2 is just all over the place. Nothing of consequence will happen for ten hours, and then five major things will happen all at once with no warning.  While all of the pieces of a great story are here, it just isn't told at the same level of efficacy as the first game in the series. I'm still interested to see where the story goes in the next installment, but nowhere near the same level as I was when I finished the first installment.  I still recommend this game to fans of the first. The battle system has some fun new additions, there are plenty of new playable characters, the music is excellent, and when the story is hitting its highest points it's a blast to play. Just don't expect the same quality as the original. 7/10 for Trails of Cold Steel 2, 9/10 for Trails of Cold Steel 1.

app_name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails of Cold Steel II
representative_review: Upon entering the last dungeon this game summed itself up perfectly:  "This feels like a final dungeon!" "Words seem to have little meaning at this point"  There are no redeeming parts to this game, no big moments whatsoever, just chunks of mini-missions you get over with while waiting for anything substantial to happen.  The whole game is modular, "paint-by-numbers".  I can't even see the developers themselves wanting to play through what they made here.  This game makes me think we've reached some sort of apex with the JRPG genre and the whole thing needs a reboot.  Mix this game engine and certain gameplay elements with "Xenogears" from PS1 and that would be the modern masterpiece everyone is looking for.  Not this embarrassment of a story.  Hoping ToCS3 can salvage this series.  *Edit* Let me make myself clear. It's quite frankly unbelievable anyone who plays this game that is older than 16 thinks it's any good.  I have a theory all the positive reviews are from guys who can't date high-level women or settle for ugly low-level women.  No hot or high-level woman would tolerate sitting around a guy playing a piece of crap RPG like this.  At least a grown man could justify playing through Sky and ToCS1.  Only an ugly girl would sit through this crap with so many cooler RPG's to play.

I recommend buying this game cause: -If you want to finish the story of the 1st game -If you want a better gameplay -if you want some good characters developments  I dont recommend buying this game if: -You are expecting a consistent good story. -You want game balance that doesnt makes all bosses HP been sponges (there is a rebalance mod out there, tho, search for it). -You dont like 40 hours of fillers, side stories, and back pedalling, that doesnt matter nor give anything important to the main story nor the characters.  I am hopping to see how trials of cold steel 3 develops the story and the gameplay.  Also Towa is the best girl.

PROS; -Nice open world -Interesting story -Good inventory system but needs some work -Spoopy -Fun with friends  CONS: -Bugged out NPCS whilst fighting -Melee not registering sometimes -Projectiles not being worth the use -Quest items spawning in the room or area you were just in and happened to spawn right in your face -NO FAST TRAVEL- In this there is a few places to repair and fix to travel the island, but there is none of these even remotely nearby the main town or areas.  [spoiler] Don't get me started on the floating black holes that teleport you or even the teleport item you get from the blindman. They only just RANDOMLY TELEPORT YOU [/spoiler]  - [spoiler] At the end of the final mission of the game. There is a puzzle that is to match these vials on the wall to the color of the RAINBOW! It is so out of place and wierd that it kinda killed the final reveal that....  [/spoiler] -[spoiler] The ending is interesting but also felt a bit undercooked as to why if the world is gone that this is a never ending cycle i guess? Called it a mile away and came away ehhh [/spoiler]  Desolate is a decent EA Title and one that is surprisingly really good and on sale with friends, its a good time for a while. app_name: FINAL FANTASY XII THE ZODIAC AGE
representative_review: Courtesy of PC emulation, I remember playing this to near-completion a few years ago, when a unified PC-centric gaming platform was still inconceivable to most of us.  Back in the day I was a rather JRPG-hungry kid, and I have fond memories of playing VII and VIII among other PC-absent gems like Dragon Quest VII and Valkyrie Profile 2.   Time has passed and two very divisive main-line entries later, it's delightful to finally revisit XII in fully renovated texturework and glorious 1080p/ 4k. This old charmer is now in great, crispy shape and still has a lot going for it!      FFXII is different from past Final Fantasies in that it offers a somewhat mature, often political-driven story with thriving characters that really grow on you. It doesn't rely too heavily on established jrpg and anime-esque tropes, which may be why a handful of people fail to appreciate its premise.  It may have alienated a few Final Fantasy X fans, but it certainly managed to attract many of those who have an eye for quality and challenging gameplay systems. It goes without saying, but it certainly also attracted those of us who were already fascinated by FF Tactic's Ivalice, its strategic gameplay and rich lore.  The tale XII has to tell takes its sweet time and may be a bit of a slow burner, but the pacing is expertly done and is tightly interwoven with its gameplay, which is surprising considering how much freedom you are given right off the bat and even when compared to XV, it is much more cohesive. I can safely say it's no slouch in that aspect.  On the port itself, there have been complaints from other players reporting game-breaking glitches though with my limited  playtime, I have yet to experience any of them and they seem to have been experienced by a loud minority. In terms of the new content, the new Zodiac system revamp should alone give old players a considerable reason to revisit this often overlooked entry in the vast Final Fantasy catalog. Adding to that, I have to really go on record to say that I was actually taken aback by the amount of care put into this port. It upholds Square-Enix's new standard for PC releases, also seen in the excellent Final Fantasy XV port which features a slew of graphical options and presets to choose from.   In conclusion, this may not necessarily be my favorite Final Fantasy, but it is a hallmark of what every RPG should aspire to be.  I just can't help but say to myself, they just don't make 'em like they used to.

representative_review: I played this game on the ps2 on non-international release and I had somewhat a good time. Not perfect but with a good walkthrough, you can pass it. Some riddles do not always make sense. -Hunts are LONG and mostly useless (you need to do them for unlock espers and stuffs but theirs rewards is nothing rewarding)  Broken: -At some locations, respawn rate for skeletons are really out of this world. -Archaeoaevis in Zertinan Caverns. -Trial mode is hard and not a lot of people will enjoy it. At no point you have time to heal or remove illness. (except on few floors) The late floor turn out to be luck based... if you don't have too much bad effect on you OR if you have too much effects on your team... just quit before changing floor. RELOAD your save game. And read walkthrough (I would never be able to complete it without knowing what coming up on the next floor). They just should have created Trial (Easy, Medium and Hard mode). -Bestiary. This is pure grinding (Killing one would be ok but they force to return multiple time and respawn area to be able to complete it. Ex: 8x Wildsnake from Giza Plains. Just one wildsnake spawn in Toam Hill (Dry) at a particular location. So move 2 area and come back 7 times. At that point., this is not playing a game. It's just torture trying to extend the game further and further. At the end, why I need to kill multiple mobs of the same type (and respawn multiple time the region)?... -Hunts - the time loss during a hunt. First you need to get the hunt. After you need to get at the petitioner location and find him/her. Find and kill the mobs. Every time, you need to return to the petitioner at his/her location. It's boring. A lot could have been done to reduce the time to GET and REDEEM a hunt. -Swords or lances can heal some monsters. Some surprise with Excalipur, Trident,... they could cure boss like Ultima...  A lot of concepts are good... trying to be more real... but a lot of them reduce the "quality of the experience for the gamer". And it's all about the "quality"... something it's like they forget to be fun to the player. Challenging yes. Enjoyable I don't think so.  And for the duration of this game: If you are explorer, you want to complete the story line, explore, get better gear, do yours licenses, get espers, some hunts and site quests. You will have around 40-60 hours of gameplay (in-game timer). And complete it at 100% (except Bestiary) would be around 80 hours.  I know there are speedrunners doing it in 2h30 to 5h (at speed x4) = around 10h-20h (with a lot of skips)

Now that 1.2 is out, let me update this review. Logistics aren't borked anymore, they work well, even though the destinations could use some work because unlocking destinations for high scale production only works up to 9 maximum destinations. If your building is supposed to deliver more you're out of luck. But I'm sure it's nothing mods won't be able to fix. Now let's give this a review shall we.  Rise of Industry falls into the economic simulation/management genre in which there is more than this game to choose from. Unlike other games in this genre - ANNO, Tropico, etc. - this game focuses on the production chains themselves. You're not building a city, you're trying to make money by selling your products.   The graphics are simple yet charming, even though some buildings look pretty similiar which makes it difficult to call them apart. That isn't necessarily bad though as everything looks absolutely beautiful together. Game seems to be pretty well optimized even though as in every simulation the later stages start to slow down.  The game features a few essential mechanics - the logistics, pollution and income, obviously. Every building has upkeep costs and placement costs. Sending products via any means - trucks, trains, zeppelins or boats - costs different amounts while offering up and downsides. Example - Zeppelins don't need to follow any streets and thus can't be stuck in traffic. Pollution is caused by using factories - farms don't cause pollution. Pollution has an effect on the growth of towns near them. (And presumably farms but I haven't tested that) Income is decided by the products you sell. Every town on the map has it's own building permit and features shops - each shop demands different products - some have higher demand which allows you to sell it for more.   The game isn't difficult per se, but has several difficulty options and can be played as either casual or hardcore. It features a sandbox mode for playing around in which the Tech Tree is fully unlocked. Talking about the Tech Tree - products have different Tiers. Base products are raw, while refining them allows for products up to Tier 3. The higher the Tier the higher you can sell it for, but it also requires more and more different products to put together as well as unlocking said products in the Tech Tree. You won't be able to sell the higher Tier products instantly as towns/cities only build new shops that demand higher Tier products as soon as you manage to supply them long enough for them to grow. Leveling up a city requires either special products or just straight up money to pay for them. Yes - towns do grow and it's a good feature, however the maps always look same-ish and could really use some sort of upgrade. Mountainranges, cities/towns that are placed on the side of said mountains, water towns/cities either straight up floating or Venedig-styled. New biomes would be a great addition as well, oceans, deserts, woods, etc. Sadly looks very same-ish so replay value is somewhat lost at that.  Your company has different 3 different products available - farm based, light industrial or heavy industrial products. This is self-explanatory.  Now to weigh the features. The AI is less than stellar. They won't be able to compete with you if you play the game as intended. The only way to challenge yourself is through the difficulty options but your AI opponents won't actually be opponents as much as they probably should be. The graphics are great, this is subjective however. Towns growing and prospering is a good feature. The logistics.. work. Its micromanagement, I enjoy, but you might not so beware. Producing and selling is satisfying. The game is finicky but you'll get used to it fairly quick.  Bugs and problems are either reported in the Steam Forums or on the official Rise of Industry discord. From what I've posted on bug reports there, the discord seems a lot better than the forums since the Developer is active on it.  You'll get what you paid for, it's a well done simulation. If you enjoy producing more than building - aka if you ever tried ANNO but dislike building a population and upgrading those - this game is worth a shot.   Here's me hoping that mods will add new products or biomes and other neat stuff. Can recommend in it's current state as I encountered no more bugs or crashes, this is subject to change as the game is still being developed though. Full price is worth it if you enjoy micromanagement and want to support the Developer, however waiting for a sale is always an option if you don't feel like spending too much.  EDIT: New features are still disappointing. Content gets stale very quickly. It's not multiplayer and mods don't do much. The game is fine, but nothing good and definitely not worth more than Factorio which goes for around $20. This game is worth $10. Recommend it during sales of at least 66% or more off. Especially with the Developer selling a DLC being a reskin even though the base game needs more content.

Imagine really bad fanfiction. Imagine it's filled with new undeveloped characters and soap-opera-liked twists. Imagine very repetitive storytelling, with lots of meaningless parts which could be removed without any damage to the story.  Congratulations, you've got yourself STEINS;GATE 0.  I am really disappointed in this one. The first part was very well-written, and the plot was build thoughtfully. Everything had a reason and some explanation and no plot-twist felt forced.  How did this happened?   And don't get me wrong, I started to play being very invested in saving Kurisu ASAP. I expected that we will see how Okarin builds his plan, but this was not it. This is 49 hours of angst of several characters and random hopping between the worldlines so Okarin could meet the spirits of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come and become brave again.   These 49 hours feel like a year, I can't believe I managed to complete this game. Such a waste of new pretty artwork.

Okay, so I really wanted to like this game since the first Steins;Gate is a masterpiece in my mind, but Steins;Gate 0 is no where near as good. I might be feeling let down due to the route I took, but I was hoping there'd be more of a pay-off after the requirements are met to reach the true ending much like the first one, instead you get a 5 minute scene that doesn't really add much. I feel similarly about the alternate endings too, they don't add much. I'm told the anime is better, so you're probably better off watching that than purchasing this game.

Long story short, it's a complete waste of time.  The pacing is bad (sloooow, just skip the audio clips and your experience will be better for it I promise), the story is incohesive - branching paths created by world line changes meaning that every time you build to any exciting climax there's no actual payoff to it, there's no satisfying ending period, and on top of that it's all completely noncanon anyways so who cares?  I don't understand why this was made and I didn't enjoy it. It has its moments I guess but they're absolutely not worth everything else around it. And even then... just go watch the original's anime, and not the VN, it's better-paced anyways.

It was sort of an underwhelming experience for me, to be honest. I was expecting this sequel to be more fast-paced, but instead it begins with lots of daily life moments that goes on and on and on. The story is a little too predictable, but maybe it is just me. Perhaps after reading the Zero Escape Series I am just immune to mild excitement.  There are also scenes where they mix (dunno if accidentally or not) portraits of both old (Steins; Gate) and new styles (Steins; Gate zero) and it looks extremely odd. At one point I was even thinking: 'Hmmm maybe they use the old art style as a hint that this character traveled from alpha world line?' but clearly that is not the case as I finish the game. So the mixed up art style is just totally confusing.   There is one character that I still don't know anything about after I finish true ending. What, then, is the purpose of introduce that character anyway? I think Steins;Gate is introducing a lot of extra characters without actually introducing them. It manages to flatten personalities of some existing characters, while introducing more flat characters.  The music does not feel as mysterious and surreal as those in the first Steins;Gate. Personally I think surreal music is one of the components that made the first Steins;Gate so outstanding.

interest and stop playing, only the metroid worked for me when it comes to those types of games, in this case metroidvanias or open sidescroller platform games, Shadow Complex has metroidvanias aspects on it but its more on the light side, you get a cool, well-designed map to explore and as you progress you find new items which may open a few new areas for you to explore and upgrades that extend quantity of usable items, but for the most part, the game is pretty linear and its not common you ending up on a area you arent supposed to be, the new items you acquire are very few in number, doesnt let this subgenre define the whole experience, I guess thats why I liked it so much, it has the traces that a metroidvania game has but it takes it very casually and lightly, its more of a inspiration for its 2d setting which imo was done extremelly well, the game is fun and the combat is amazing, graphics and arstyle for a game of its time were done well, altho the story is serviceable at best it doesnt get in the way of the addicting gameplay but its not a bad story at all, just cliche, with a few fine twists, its competent, the game also has a good soundtrack and the duration of the game doesnt overstay its welcome like many similar games do, theres also some good action setpieces and boss battles that keeps the pacing fresh, I loved my time with Shadow Complex, played in a The story is laughable, the characters are poorly written, the gameplay is clunky and plagued with countless issues, the music is meh, the pacing is horrific, and worst of all it completely ruins everything about the metroidvania subgenre. This game could be completely linear and nothing about it would have been different. It has you follow a little blue line through the rooms and absolutely nothing about its design encourages any exploration. It would take me hours to write out all of the issues in this game and I could still continue. Frankly I don't want to talk about this game anymore. I'll leave you with this: if you like metroidvania play Hollow Knight, Dead Cells, Axiom Verge, or really anything else before coming to this game.

It was pretty disappointing. The game is very poorly optimized, my machine that can run Homeworld: Cataclysm on Maximum detail still hard cursor lag in this game that didn't seem to go away regardless of what the settings were set to; possibly a symptom of the frame-rate being locked too low. For a platformer the jumping and collision detection is very irritating, where the main character (who is a "regular joe that can jump 2m straight up without trying) seems to bounce up and down like a spring with no hang-time but also seems to drift slightly when you're trying to guide him into moving. The game is pretty but when zoomed it it's easy to see there's something wrong with how the models are laid out and that the objects they're touching don't seem to collide with their hands, even if the publisher couldn't figure out the technical issues, it seems like better framing in the cutscenes should have been used to hide these problems.  Other reviewers have already posted about the flood of enemies, the similar looking levels (which are otherwise fairly pretty), and the questionable design. But what I really hated was the plot. It's not just cringe inducing but the main character has zero-agency. A total pawn being manipulated by the people around him, or given his apparent denseness a tool metaphor would be more appropriate (like a hammer (bluntly)); once the plot twists start unraveling the game doesn't provide a good reason for you to play along with them instead of just leaving these idiots to go at it and heading home by yourself.   I didn't finish, but I did read about the ending online, and it was basically what I expected.

[h1]Overview[/h1] Shadow Complex (Remastered) is a 2D sidescrolling platformer game. The story of the game is simple: you go explore a cave and then your wife is abducted. You must find her. The main character is the most one dimensional being ever, he is the epitome of a cliche white man hero. You come a cross a futuristic facility which you make your way through, obtaining new gear and weapons along the way. There are secrets littered around the place which you can find as well.  [h1]Opinions[/h1]  The shooting mechanics in this game are janky. Awful. You encounter enemies which are out of bound or off screen and therefore you can't shoot them.   The movement in this game is also janky. Sometimes it is impossible to drop down while ledge grabbing. The movement feels weird and unresponsive. The wall jumping is as bad as ever.  The gameplay of this game couldn't be any more repetive. You go through room after room of the same things, doing the same stuff. Shoot the people, done, next room. And the backtracking. The backtracking in this game is so awful, you have to do the exact same rooms again, just to find an item which grants extra grenade capacity. Grenades? Useless item.  The graphics are so unstylish and every room ends up looking no different than the last.   I can't even remember what the music sounds like. It's forgettable.  I had a horrid time with this game. I'm quite the fan of 2D platformers, but EVERY SINGLE mechanic in this game feels incredibly unpolished and janky.  [h1]Pros[/h1] [list] [*] I can't think of any positive aspects. [/list]  [h1]Cons[/h1] [list] [*] The Graphics [*] The combat [*] The Gameplay [*] The music [*] The controls [*] The story [*] Repetitive [*] Monotonous [*] Tedious [*] Samey  [*] The backtracking! [*] Takes too long to acquire any useful items and get anywhere in this game [/list]  [h1]Neutral[/h1] [list] [*] The graphics are slightly pretty, and the game is fun for the first half an hour.  [/list]  [h1]Conclusion[/h1] I absolutely cannot recommend this game. In my experience it was dreadful and a quick uninstall for me. 2/10 - a waste of time

app_name: 三国群英传8 Heroes of the Three Kingdoms 8
representative_review: The game plays differently from previous iterations and the graphics are good improvements.          I don't recommend the reviews from players who only played for a short time and simply get overwhelmed by expectations. There is always some sort of learning curve to a new system and game mechanics. The Dev should definitely have opened a demo version as most of the negative reviews are based on their first impression and a subpar tutorial. Something like the solo system has already been revealed much earlier and is still a big pain point for reviewers going into the game.   There are things that can definitely be tweaked and many quality of life updates that can be made. Knowing that there has probably been limited play tests it is understandable but should be patched.  Things to improve on includes but not limited to: 1) Map movement speed too slow 2) Command icons are way too small.      Battle icon.                Minion command icon very difficult to notice               Unable to filter general vs minion               The solo battle icon on the mid top screen is pretty unnoticeable               Ability Icon               Ability cast color blends into the background a bit              Hot Keys could be explained better (F, 1,2,3, f1 ,F2, space, enter, Z etc)       Big Map                   Command Icon on the top left                                If you haven't played the previous games and didn't know to rank up generals then you won't even notice it up there. Diplomacy also.                  Some of the automation commands are less noticeable (Button UI)                   Select and deselect using esc is pretty funky as it often calls the setting menu        Castle options                   Sub options like constructions are pretty small                   Unclear how recruiting minion option is located unlike previous versions  3) Bring back Himiko XD. Unless you need to unlock her like the 4th gen 4) You should allow selection of any number DLC character and not recruit all vs recruit non. 5) A lack of a minimap can be a problem 6) Could bring back the yearly tournament feature  The battle system I enjoyed. It lacked things from past generations but I can see good things that could be added to the current system.   If you find it too easy then try hard difficulty and buff minions. Mid campaign the difficulty ramps up but there can definitely be some number tweaks. Level up and recruit higher star minions to help with fights later.
